observations.body: Peter addresses Israel, names Jesus’ works, crucifixion, resurrection, Davidic Scripture, exaltation, the Father’s promise, and the outpouring the crowd sees and hears.
observations.label: Peter moves from Jesus’ death and resurrection to the visible outpouring

observations.body: The passage presents Attesting, killing, raising, exalting, receiving, and pouring as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: Attesting, killing, raising, exalting, receiving, and pouring

observations.body: The passage places What you now see and hear beside Attesting, killing, raising, exalting, receiving, and pouring.
observations.label: What you now see and hear

payload.posture: Read Acts 2:22–36 as one movement in Pentecost, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states peter addresses Israel, names Jesus’ works, crucifixion, resurrection, Davidic Scripture, exaltation, the Father’s promise, and the outpouring the crowd sees and hears. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Pentecost.
payload.title: Peter moves from Jesus’ death and resurrection to the visible outpouring
